label_points.latin: Musculus transversus perinei profundus (smooth-muscle plate per authors)
Musculus transversus perinei profundus (smooth-muscle plate per authors)

key_findings: 'Perineal muscle shape and location from nine cadavers (five males; average age, 79 years) were macroscopically examined.' 'An overall layered perineum structure was revealed in both sexes. A slender, band-like striated muscle was observed near the surface. Beneath this layer was a dense connective tissue membrane that provides separation. A triangular, plate-like shaped smooth muscle with transversely oriented fibers occupied the deep perineal space, which, unlike the striated muscle, was continuous with the rectal wall and was identified as the deep transverse perineal muscle.'
clinical_relevance: 'Findings indicate that the deep transverse perineal muscle may be a distinct pelvic smooth muscle component.' Relevant to the classic 'urogenital diaphragm' concept, to perineal/obstetric repair and to transperineal surgery (layer-by-layer anatomy).
notes: Sci Rep 2025, CC BY 4.0. Same group (Muro/Akita, Tokyo) as PMC8373982, PMC6942605, PMC7182620, PMC12003430. Fig 1 panels A-B are the male SUPERFICIAL POUCH; C = PERINEAL MEMBRANE; D = DEEP POUCH. Fig 7 is the authors' own schematic (good for the 'layers' slide). The interpretation of the DTP as smooth muscle is the authors' view (contrast PMC13069139).

key_findings: 'Investigations were performed on embalmed human donors of both sexes (n = 10, mean age at death: 82 years).' 'A relatively thick tissue plate (diameter: 4-5 mm) located superior to a fascia-like structure, the perineal membrane, was observed running transversally to the ischiopubic rami. Macroscopically, a clearly visible transverse running muscle was not observed in both sexes.' 'In both sexes, the volume densities of the connective tissue were approximately 80%.' 'In females, the proportion of the striated muscle cells was less than 1%.'
clinical_relevance: 'There was no evidence of the existence of a clearly definable striated DTP muscle, not only in females but also in males. Muscle cells decreased with increasing age.' Supports teaching the deep pouch as a fibromuscular plate rather than a distinct striated 'urogenital diaphragm'.
notes: J Anat 2025, CC BY 4.0. Fig 3 (posterior/inner view) downloaded, viewed and deleted (crowded numbering, hard to read). Fig 1 also shows the anal triangle (ischioanal fossa) - overlap with the anal-triangle agent only as context. Numbers in the images are white digits.

key_findings: 'In this study, seven male corpses of body donors were used to conduct macroscopic anatomy, histology, and three-dimensional reconstruction. The Cowper's gland was surrounded laterally and posterosuperiorly by striated and smooth muscles, respectively. The striated muscle bundle was connected from the superficial transverse perineal muscle, levator ani, and external anal sphincter to the external urethral sphincter (rhabdosphincter). The smooth muscle was part of the deep transverse perineal muscle and entered between the bilateral Cowper's glands and lobules.'
clinical_relevance: 'Our findings indicate that the secretion and emission of the Cowper's gland in humans are carried out through the cooperation of striated and smooth muscles.' Bulbourethral glands sit in the deep pouch at the bulb - relevant to bulbar urethroplasty and APR/perineal prostatectomy planes.
notes: Sci Rep 2021, CC BY 4.0. Only cadaver photo of the bulbourethral gland in situ found in the OA bucket. Fig 2 is the best single image of PM + deep pouch contents (male).

key_findings: 'The pelvic floor muscles of 28 pelvic halves from 16 female cadavers (mean age 79.75 years) were dissected'. 'The bulbospongiosus muscle was found to be attached to the lateral surface of the external anal sphincter. The superficial transverse perineal muscle crossed superiorly to the bulbospongiosus and coursed medially toward its contralateral muscle bundle deep to the anterior portion of the external anal sphincter. The superficial transverse perineal muscle formed the middle sling.'
clinical_relevance: 'This study proposes that three muscular slings could be important in supporting the pelvic floor in women.' Challenges the textbook 'all muscles insert into the perineal body' model - relevant to perineal repair after obstetric tears.
notes: Anat Sci Int 2019, CC BY 4.0. Fig 2 (inferior view) not used here (dark; adds little beyond Fig 3/4) - file kept in the folder because the anal-triangle agent uses it. Fig 4 is small (708x226) but both panels are legible; panel B used for label points.

'In the crus of the clitoris, about 12 such bundles can be recognized while about 32 bundles are present in the clitoral hemi-body.' 'clitoris has approximately 6 times denser innervation compared to the penis.' Specimens: 'Formalin-fixed vulva samples were collected from 6 female cadavers'.

key_findings: 'We dissected the ligaments providing the suspension of the penis in 7 formalized corpses.' 'We have identified three types of fundiform ligament: A unique triangular structure; A double structure accompanied by accessory fascicles; A ligament structure with the aspect of an undifferentiated fibrous connective band.' 'For the suspensory ligament, we identified three groups of fibers through which it is attached to the penile body.' 'the suspensory ligament is represented by three blades: two superficial blades sharing the role of the fundiform ligament and a deep blade on the midline, which is continued by the deep fascia of the penis'.
clinical_relevance: Ligament sectioning in penile lengthening risks the dorsal neurovascular bundle and penile instability; the fundiform ligament is a derivative of the membranous layer of the abdominal superficial fascia (Scarpa) - the Scarpa-Colles-dartos continuum at the penile root.
notes: Basic Clin Androl 2023, CC BY 4.0. Closest OA cadaver material to the 'fascia penis / Scarpa continuity' topic. Fig 1 (unexplained numbers in caption) and Fig 12 (dorsal NV bundle - pudendal territory of another agent) downloaded, viewed, deleted. The caption of Fig 5 lists numbers; '4/5' spermatic cords are the tubular structures lateral to the penis.

topic: Sex differences of the deep pouch: rhabdosphincter, compressor urethrae, urethrovaginal sphincter, perineal membrane, Cowper's gland, DTP (author diagrams)
title: The Urethral Rhabdosphincter, Levator Ani Muscle, and Perineal Membrane: A Review

figures.label: Figure 11
figures.caption: A diagram of the levator ani, rhabdosphincter, and perineal membrane in women. Lateral view through the bony pelvis. In the female, the rhabdosphincter is connected with the ischiadic bony ramus by the perineal membrane. The fibers of the levator ani muscle are directed to the external sphincter and anus. In the female, the rhabdosphincter is continuous with the anterior long muscle sheet, the urethrovaginal sphincter (UVS), and the posterolateral small part, the compressor urethrae (CU). These striated muscles are embedded in an elastic-fiber mesh that provides the insertion for the perineal membrane (PM) to the ischiadic bony ramus. The perineal membrane extends anteromedially to a space between the vestibular bulb and the vaginal wall. The levator ani is attached to the superior aspects of the perineal membrane (arrows).
figures.what_it_shows: Female, lateral view through the bony pelvis: rhabdosphincter (RS) around the urethra, compressor urethrae (CU) and urethrovaginal sphincter (UVS) continuous with the thick perineal membrane (PM) that anchors them to the ischiopubic ramus; levator ani attaches to the upper surface of the PM; vestibular bulb and bulbospongiosus below.
figures.labels_visible_in_image: Uterus, Bladder, Vagina, Pubis, RS, CU, Levator ani (x2), Urethra, PM, UVS, External anal sphincter, Vestibular bulb, Bulbospongiosus muscle, Anus

figures.label: Figure 10
figures.caption: A diagram of the levator ani and rhabdosphincter in men. Lateral view through the bony pelvis. In the male, the rhabdosphincter is connected with the inferomedial margin of the levator ani. The fibers of the levator ani muscle are directed to the external sphincter and anus. By a thick fascia (sandwiched by arrows) containing veins, nerves, elastic fibers, and smooth muscle, the rhabdosphincter area in the male is connected with the inferomedial margin of the levator ani. Stars indicate a layer for the male perineal membrane (not drawn; see Figure 2(c) insert). On the lower side of the rhabdosphincter area, the deep transverse perineal muscle connects Cowper's gland and the internal surface of the ischiadic bone.
figures.what_it_shows: Male, lateral view: rhabdosphincter (RS) around the membranous urethra continuing up as prostatocapsular RS, Cowper's gland in the deep pouch below RS, deep transverse perineal muscle behind it, levator ani lateral with veins and nerves between; stars = connection of RS to perineal muscles.
figures.labels_visible_in_image: Prostatocapsular RS, Bladder, Pubis, Prostate, RS, Levator ani, Veins and nerves, Urethra, Cowper's gland, Deep transverse perineal muscle, External anal sphincter, Anus, stars

key_findings: Review of the authors' serial-section studies in elderly cadavers: 'The male perineal membrane was thin but solid and extends along the inferior margin or bottom of the rhabdosphincter area. In contrast, the female rhabdosphincter, including the compressor urethrae and urethrovaginal sphincter muscles, was embedded in the elastic fiber mesh that is continuous with the thick, multilaminar perineal membrane. The inferomedial edge of the female LA was attached to the upper surface of the perineal membrane and not directly attached to the rhabdosphincter.'
clinical_relevance: Continence anatomy for radical prostatectomy and female anti-incontinence surgery: 'We presented new diagrams showing the gender differences in topographical anatomy of the LA and rhabdosphincter.'
notes: Biomed Res Int 2014, CC BY 3.0. Author diagrams (no cadaver photo of CU/UVS exists in the OA bucket); histology figures of the same article not used (cross-sectional).

key_findings: 'Pelvises from five female cadavers were collected for histological analysis.' 'The female urethra was surrounded by four muscle layers arranged from inner to outer layers in the following order: longitudinal smooth muscle, circular smooth muscle, the external urethral sphincter (EUS), and an outermost smooth muscle layer.'
